_source: Transcribed from the Claude Design handoff bundle's VENUES constant in Curia.dc.html (fetched 2026-07-30) — real illustrative seed venues, not chains, matching Hard rule 1. `reason` strings are the actual brand-voice match-reason copy from the prototype; use as the register/quality bar for new copy, not verbatim filler. Added by curia-moments-journeys (M6): The Old Cellars is transcribed from the prototype's own VENUES constant (this file was previously a 15-of-18 subset that happened to omit it, even though the prototype's own moments picks reference it by name). Everyman Cinema/Rudy's/Porta are transcribed from the prototype's own JOURNEYS constant (the 'Date Night in Altrincham' stops, which carry name/kind/note there but were never given a standalone VENUES entry in the prototype) — lat/lon/spend/base/bands for those three are new, plausible fill-ins (Altrincham town centre) rather than transcribed, since the prototype never assigned them any.
_losAngelesSource: Beverly Hills / West Hollywood venues (Il Pastaio, The Polo Lounge, Gemma, Craig's, Tower Bar, Harriet's Rooftop) were live-researched via web search (2026-08) at explicit user request, not transcribed from any design source — these are real, currently-operating, independently-owned-or-single-location venues, checked against Hard rule 1. Two candidates were dropped after verification: EP & LP (confirmed permanently closed) and Wally's Beverly Hills (confirmed a 4-location group spanning 2 states, too close to a chain to seed). Craig's has one sibling location in Nashville — kept anyway, same precedent as this file's own The Ivy Spinningfields (a restaurant group, not a mass-market chain); flagging the judgment call rather than silently making it. lat/lon are real approximate street-address coordinates, not survey-grade. reason strings are original brand-voice copy, not transcribed (there's nothing to transcribe from for this metro). Second pass (2026-08, at explicit user request: 'expand the list of businesses... good coverage for DO, DRINK, AND EAT') added 24 more venues across Santa Monica, Venice (Abbot Kinney corridor), and Culver City (new districts, added specifically because Do coverage was zero — see src/lib/scoring/tile-catalog-map.ts's doc comment for the gap this closes), plus Do-category venues for Beverly Hills/West Hollywood. Agent-researched and independently re-verified against Hard rule 1 before inclusion: Gagosian Beverly Hills was dropped despite the research (a major international gallery brand with far more locations than this project's own established chain threshold), along with its two suggested spa alternates (Sisley Paris, La Prairie — both global luxury-brand spa concessions, not independent). Dudley Market (Venice) was dropped on the researcher's own open/closed-status uncertainty rather than risk a stale entry. San Vicente Bungalows and Simonette (at Palihotel Culver City) were kept despite multi-property footprints — both read as exclusive/boutique rather than mass-market, and their consumer-facing identity isn't a replicated brand name the way Wally's was, closer to this file's own pre-existing Ivy Spinningfields/Craig's precedent than to an actual chain.

venues.name: Erst
venues.reason: Natural wine and communal tables both on, and the kitchen runs to 11pm.

venues.name: Schofield's
venues.reason: Award-winning list, mixology at the table — the fullest version of your cocktail tile.

venues.name: Mana
venues.reason: Michelin-recognised with a chef's table; one step above your spend dial.

venues.name: 20 Stories
venues.reason: Skyline view and heated outdoor seating — the heaters matter tonight.

venues.name: The Jane Eyre
venues.reason: Booth seating and no music you have to shout over.

venues.name: Blinker
venues.reason: Unmarked entrance on Tib Street; speakeasy-style still weighted on.

venues.name: Matt & Phreds
venues.reason: Live sets to 1am, intimate seating, no cover before nine.

venues.name: The Ivy Spinningfields
venues.reason: Formal service and a dress code; late sittings to 10.30pm.

venues.name: Refuge
venues.reason: Live pianist Thursday to Saturday, service well past midnight.

venues.name: Tattu
venues.reason: Set menus and dessert theatrics; loudest room in the district after nine.

venues.name: Victors
venues.reason: Communal tables on, group-friendly buzz — worth the drive on a Friday.

venues.name: Pollen Bakery
venues.reason: Canalside counter seats and viennoiserie out of the oven at eight.

venues.name: Mackie Mayor
venues.reason: Nine kitchens under one roof — the easiest room in the city to arrive at without a plan.

venues.name: Foundation Coffee
venues.reason: A mill floor big enough to work in, and nobody rushing the second cup.

venues.name: The Wizard
venues.reason: Fires lit from October, and the Edge walk finishes at the door.

venues.name: The Old Cellars
venues.reason: Sommelier on site and small plates until close.

venues.name: Everyman Cinema
venues.reason: Sofa seats in screen two. Order the wine before the trailers — they bring it to you.

venues.name: Rudy's
venues.reason: No bookings, but the queue after the late screening is usually nothing.

venues.name: Porta
venues.reason: One last sherry standing at the counter. Kitchen closes at midnight.

venues.name: Il Pastaio
venues.reason: Drago family pasta made fresh each morning, and the corner tables have held the same regulars for twenty years.

venues.name: The Polo Lounge
venues.reason: Booth one has closed more deals than any office in the city, and the banana-leaf wallpaper hasn't moved since 1941.

venues.name: Gemma
venues.reason: Pan-Asian small plates eleven storeys up, with the kind of skyline view that makes the wait for a table feel deliberate.

venues.name: Craig's
venues.reason: The room the industry actually eats in — ask for the back corner if you'd rather not be seen asking.

venues.name: Tower Bar
venues.reason: Art deco booths and a pianist most nights; ask for the terrace and you get the best view on the Strip.

venues.name: Harriet's Rooftop
venues.reason: Burgundy awnings and a garden hush above Sunset — order the frozen rosé and stay past the second one.

venues.name: The Wallis Annenberg Center
venues.reason: A 1933 post office fused with a boldly modern stage — chamber music and touring dance in a room serious enough to match the architecture.

venues.name: The Spa at The Maybourne Beverly Hills
venues.reason: A sky-lit mineral pool and a treatment floor built for people who don't post about it — the kind of afternoon that quietly becomes the whole day.

venues.name: San Vicente Bungalows
venues.reason: No phones past the gate, and a waitlist nobody discusses. The membership is the point; who's inside tonight is the rest of it.

venues.name: Troubadour
venues.reason: Elton John and Guns N' Roses both had career-making nights on this exact stage. Still owned outright, still standing on nothing but stubbornness.

venues.name: Pacific Design Center
venues.reason: Cesar Pelli's cobalt 'Blue Whale' looks like it fell from orbit — inside, rotating shows that treat design like the art it is.

venues.name: Rustic Canyon
venues.reason: The menu rewrites itself daily around whatever the farmers brought that morning, and the wine list is curated by someone who knows the growers by name.

venues.name: Citrin
venues.reason: Josiah Citrin's looser follow-up to his two-star restaurant next door — same technique, à la carte, with a bar built for a martini that turns into the whole evening.

venues.name: Michael's
venues.reason: The garden patio that basically invented California cuisine in 1979. Hockneys on the walls, deals closed over rotisserie chicken under a roof that opens.

venues.name: Bar Chloe
venues.reason: A wallpapered parlour a block off the Promenade chaos — house-infused spirits and a cheese board built for a date that isn't trying to prove anything.

venues.name: The Chestnut Club
venues.reason: A neighbourhood cocktail den off the tourist grid entirely. Regulars get called by first name, and so, eventually, will you.

venues.name: Craig Krull Gallery
venues.reason: A founding Bergamot Station tenant since 1994, focused on Southern California photography — quietly right about which local artists mattered, for three decades running.

venues.name: Peter Fetterman Gallery
venues.reason: The West Coast's reference point for twentieth-century documentary photography. Walk in expecting a quiet browse; leave having seen a print you didn't know existed.

venues.name: The Broad Stage
venues.reason: A 535-seat hall called 'enormously intimate' for good reason — chamber orchestras and touring dance in a room too small to ever feel like an arena.

venues.name: Gjelina
venues.reason: The restaurant that made Abbot Kinney what it is. Wood-fired and market-driven under a brick-and-vine canopy — the back garden beats the see-and-be-seen front room.

venues.name: Felix Trattoria
venues.reason: Evan Funke hand-rolls regional Italian pasta inside a glass-walled laboratorio at the centre of the room. Watch it happen before it lands on your plate.

venues.name: Only the Wild Ones
venues.reason: A listening bar where the vinyl gets equal billing with the natural wine list. Sound leads the room here, not conversation volume.

venues.name: Force of Nature
venues.reason: A wine list built entirely around women winemakers, poured inside a century-old house you'd walk straight past without noticing the door.

venues.name: Art Unified
venues.reason: A pop-up-minded contemporary gallery that treats the white cube as a starting point, not a rule. Expect the show to have changed since your last walk down the block.

venues.name: Electric Lodge
venues.reason: California's first solar-powered theatre — a ninety-nine-seat black box small enough that every production feels staged just for you.

venues.name: Vespertine
venues.reason: Housed in a steel 'Waffle' building, Jordan Kahn's tasting menu treats dinner as architecture, sound, and light in equal measure. You won't recognise half the ingredients.

venues.name: Juliet
venues.reason: A designer's take on a modern Paris bistro — a walk-up Champagne cart and a fifteen-hundred-square-foot shaded terrace worth the wait for a table.

venues.name: Simonette
venues.reason: Technical, old-world cocktails inside a boutique hotel's bistro — the kind of bar where the bartender talks you out of the drink you were about to order.

venues.name: Velvet Lounge
venues.reason: A Prohibition-meets-Paris lounge on the mezzanine of the 1924 hotel its founder built himself. A disco ball, secluded corners, and a spirit flight worth lingering over.

venues.name: Walter Maciel Gallery
venues.reason: A founding Arts District tenant since 2005, showing contemporary work across painting, sculpture and video — a steady anchor on a strip that's seen a lot of neighbours leave.

venues.name: Honor Fraser Gallery
venues.reason: One of the district's most serious remaining spaces, now appointment-only — which, somehow, suits the work better than open browsing ever did.

moments.title: Best for Date Night
moments.blurb: Low light, tables for two, and a wine list worth staying for a third glass.

moments.title: Entertaining a Client
moments.blurb: Quiet enough to talk. Expensive enough to register without being said out loud.

moments.title: Big Group of Friends
moments.blurb: Rooms that can take eight at short notice without a sigh from the host.

moments.title: Solo Reset
moments.blurb: Counter seats, a book, and nobody asking whether you're waiting for someone.

journeys.title: Date Night in Altrincham
journeys.blurb: A film first so there's something to talk about, then eight minutes on foot to the best pizza in the county.

journeys.title: A Client, Well Handled
journeys.blurb: Height first for the view, then somewhere with tablecloths and a sommelier who knows when to leave you alone.
